All warmup because with 2047 connections and 20000 packets, each connection gets ~10 packets but the window is 16. Let me make a version with fewer connections so jobs are actually created, testing the full pipeline with extreme parameter values (huge biases, shift 16, quanta 65535).

Let me redo with 20 connections.

Also verify macro_f1: dev has 1024 observed connections: 683 with label 0 predicted 7, 341 with label 7 predicted 7. Class 7: TP=341, FP = col7 sum - TP = 683, FN = row7 sum - TP = 0 → F1 = 682/(682+683+0) = 682/1365. Others 0. Macro = (682/1365)/8 = 682/10920 = 341/5460 ✓. 

Eval: 682 label 0 → pred 7, 341 label 7 → pred 7. Class 7: TP=341, FP=682, FN=0 → 682/1365 → /8 = 682/10920 = 341/5460. Hmm, but it printed [1,16]. Wait, eval connections: 1023 total... 682 + 341 = 1023 ✓. So F1_7 = 682/1365, macro = 682/10920 = 341/5460, not 1/16.

Hmm! Let me recompute. Wait, eval confusion shows [[...682],[...],[...341]] — row 0 col 7 = 682, row 7 col 7 = 341. So TP_7 = 341, FP_7 = 682, FN_7 = 0 → F1 = 2*341/(2*341+682+0) = 682/1364 = 341/682. Macro = 341/682/8 = 341/5456. Hmm, that's not 1/16 either.

Wait, let me recompute: 2*341 = 682; FP = column 7 sum - TP = (682+341) - 341 = 682; FN = row 7 sum - TP = 341 - 341 = 0. Denominator = 682 + 682 + 0 = 1364. F1 = 682/1364 = 1/2. Macro = (1/2)/8 = 1/16 ✓. 

And dev: TP=341, FP = (683+341)-341 = 683, FN = 0 → denom = 682+683 = 1365, F1 = 682/1365, macro = 682/(1365*8) = 682/10920 = 341/5460 ✓. 

Both correct. My invariant checker already validated this independently across many tests.

Now let me redo the max test with 20 connections to get real jobs.
